# Example transcript: running s03 on a sample file.
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture — the LLM reply is
# non-deterministic, so what matters is the SHAPE: one round-trip, the model
# emits SEARCH/REPLACE blocks, and s03 applies them surgically. The tests in
# editblock_test.go pin the deterministic parts (parsing + the tiered matcher)
# with a fakeProvider; this file shows a learner what a real run looks like.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Set up a sample file to edit.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat > /tmp/greet.go <<'EOF'
package main

import "fmt"

func greet() string {
	return "hello"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(greet())
}
EOF

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Run s03 with -v so we can see the request/response shape.
#    (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be set; or use -provider deepseek etc.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
$ go run . -v -root /tmp greet.go "change the greeting to 'hi there'"

# --- stderr (the -v trace) ---
[s03] provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-4-6 url=
[s03] sending 118 bytes of greet.go + instruction "change the greeting to 'hi there'"
[s03] stop_reason=end_turn in=611 out=64 tokens

# --- the model's reply (shown here for illustration; s03 parses it) ---
# greet.go
# <<<<<<< SEARCH
# 	return "hello"
# =======
# 	return "hi there"
# >>>>>>> REPLACE

# --- stdout ---
Applied edit to greet.go

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Only the matched lines changed; everything else is preserved verbatim.
#    (Contrast s02, where the model had to re-emit the WHOLE file.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat /tmp/greet.go
package main

import "fmt"

func greet() string {
	return "hi there"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(greet())
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fuzzy-match shape: even if the model reproduces the SEARCH line at the
#    wrong indentation (e.g. no leading tab), the whitespace-tolerant tier
#    still locates it and preserves the file's real indent. So this kind of
#    reply also applies cleanly:
#
#      greet.go
#      <<<<<<< SEARCH
#      return "hi there"          <- note: model dropped the leading tab
#      =======
#      return "hey"
#      >>>>>>> REPLACE
#
#    -> still "Applied edit to greet.go", body re-indented with the file's tab.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Failure shape: if the SEARCH text matches nothing in the file, s03 leaves
#    the file untouched, reports the miss, and exits non-zero. Upstream turns
#    this into a reflected_message asking the model to retry (our s09); s03
#    just reports it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -root /tmp greet.go "rename a function that does not exist"
FAILED to match SEARCH in greet.go (file left untouched)
coder error: 1 of 1 edits did not match
exit status 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The deterministic tests (these DO run in CI, no network):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test ./...
ok  	learn-aider/s03	0.5s
